scope: Proposition 3.2 (Uniform product-circuit compilation) of the manuscript “Variable-dimension Weisfeiler–Leman equivalence on general and subcubic graphs” (preprints/Variable-dimension-Weisfeiler-Leman-equivalence-on-general-and-subcubic-graphs-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 133 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 5b3048ce062b1b8e), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 9. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a deterministic one-tape machine M with the initialization and frozen-halting convention just specified, and an integer polynomial p satisfying p(m) ≥ m + 2 and bounding its running time by 2p(m). For every word w of length m, one can generate a product description in the sense of Definition 3.1 of a finite acyclic circuit at address length r = 2(p(m) + 2), with scalar terminal tests, such that at least one test is true if and only if M accepts w. There are OM (1) gate types and OM ((r+1)2 +m) connection schemas and seed or test requests, each with r constant-size coordinate entries. All domains have nonempty binary factors and all coordinate maps are injections. The total number of coordinate entries is OM (r((r+1)2 +m)). The description is generated deterministically in time polynomial in r + m, with constants depending only on M, p, without enumerating times or full addresses.
